business_scope.primary_industry_name: Digital Magazine Publishing and Sponsored Media Placements

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code tradition with autonomous commercial law codification – Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–United States DTA (3 April 1996, as amended by Protocol 2004)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); CSSF Regulation No 17-03 of 3 February 2017; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 3 February 2017 on AML/CFT; Luxembourg Criminal Code and FIU (CRF) reporting obligations.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal (RBE access restricted following ECJ joined cases C-37/20 and C-601/20 WM/Sovim of 22 November 2022; only public authorities, FIU, obliged entities performing CDD, and persons with legitimate interest may access UBO data)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each natural person (shareholder, manager, UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority or notary of country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney authorizing Luxembourg incorporation counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in country of origin or Luxembourg notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of registered office address / domiciliation agreement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg certified domiciliation company (agréé by Ministry of Justice)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds evidence (3 months bank statements)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank in home or EU jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or notarized certification (CSSF Reg. 17-03 standard)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory per CSSF Reg. 17-03 and AML Law of 12 November 2004: (i) PEP status screening of all UBOs, directors, and managers; (ii) continuous screening against EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions, US OFAC SDN list, and UK HMT consolidated list; (iii) adverse media and negative news checks; (iv) enhanced due diligence (EDD) triggered by any PEP flag, sanctions match, or adverse media; (v) immediate suspicious transaction reporting to the Luxembourg FIU (Cellule de Renseignement Financier – CRF); (vi) annual re-screening of existing UBOs and managers; (vii) preservation of screen evidence for five years post-business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – www.lbr.lu (RCS, Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés); name reservation effected via MyGuichet.lu / LBR e-services
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company name must use Latin script; permitted languages are Luxembourgish, French, German, or English; SARL must display legal form suffix 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or 'S.à r.l.' / 'SARL'; name must be distinguishable from existing RCS entries and must not mislead as to activity, size, or legal form; foreign-language transliterations retained in Latin characters; accented characters accepted subject to RCS normalization rules.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: État / État de Luxembourg / Luxembourg State
Prestataire de services de paiement / Payment Services
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the LBR refuses a name reservation, the applicant must request written grounds. An administrative claim (recours gracieux) is filed with the Ministry of Justice within three months of refusal, accompanied by an amended denomination or evidence of distinctiveness. A subsequent judicial appeal (recours contentieux) is permitted within three months before the Tribunal administratif (Luxembourg Administrative Court). Extensions of a reservation are not granted; after expiry, a fresh name reservation application must be submitted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Allowed – a digital publishing SARL may use a Ministry of Justice certified domiciliation provider as its registered seat. However, under the Law of 26 July 2019 on shell company transparency and Luxembourg tax residence rules, genuine economic substance must be demonstrable: Luxembourg-based management decisions, operational oversight of the digital magazine platform, client documentation, and risk management. A pure letterbox arrangement without local substance risks denial of Luxembourg tax residence and potential foreign tax authority reclassification.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low_Risk – approximately 15% annual probability for a low-risk digital publishing entity with no regulated license, no government concession, and no high-risk jurisdictions in the ownership chain. Unannounced on-site inspections by the RCS registration authority, tax authorities, or domiciliation supervisor may occur, especially where the domiciliation provider hosts more than 50 companies at one address.

Notarial deed of incorporation (statutes, share capital declaration, management appointment)

RESA legal publication of incorporation deed and statutes

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary / translation bureau / competent ministry of foreign affairs (country of origin)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / domiciliation service (annual, prorated for incorporation year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Justice certified domiciliation provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark EUR 120–180 per month including registered agent duties

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate and AML legal counsel professional fees (structure review, AML/KYC, UBO declarations)
KYC/AML screening engine – PEP and international sanctions screening (initial + annual cycle)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 180 et seq. (Société à Responsabilité Limitée); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Registry (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés); Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Registry (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), District Court of Luxembourg, national electronic portal e-RCS / lbr.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (Acte constitutif et statuts notariés) together with the RCS application form and statement of authorized signatories.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed capital is EUR 12,000. The full capital must be subscribed and paid up in cash before notarization. The cash contribution is blocked in an escrow account held by a Luxembourg credit institution or notary, released upon execution of the notarial deed; the notary certifies receipt and the RCS verifies the bank certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: This first written founding resolution of the sole founding shareholder and, as the case may be, of the initial general meeting of [COMPANY] S.à r.l. resolves: 1. The equity capital of EUR 12,000 as stated in the articles is deemed fully subscribed and paid in by the subscribers listed in the notarial deed. 2. The registered office of the company is fixed at [ADDRESS] in the District of Luxembourg. 3. [MANAGER NAME] is appointed manager (Gérant) of the Company with power to act alone on behalf of the company in all matters, including banking, tax, and registry issues. [ALTERNATE] is appointed replacement manager in the manager’s absence. 4. The manager is instructed and authorized to register the Company with the RCS, open bank accounts, publish the deed, and file all necessary tax and social declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit share capital and execute notarized articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary admitted in Luxembourg (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg) and a licensed Luxembourg credit institution for the escrow account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account in the name of the future company at a Luxembourg bank. Deposit at least EUR 12,000 and obtain a bank certificate of capital deposit. Then appear before a Luxembourg notary with all shareholders and managers; the notary reviews the draft articles, performs name and corporate-object checks, and executes the notarial deed. The notary will subsequently forward the deed for electronic registration with the RCS.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate proving deposit of EUR 12,000 into the blocked account
Valid passports or national identity cards of all shareholders and managers
Signed powers of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a legal obstacle, such as a name conflict, invalid object, or capital deficiency, the parties must amend the draft, cure the capital proof, or select an alternative company name, then reschedule execution. A supplemental notarial declaration can be recorded without restarting the entire process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation application with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL), Luxembourg, via the electronic e-RCS portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, file the RCS registration dossier through the notary’s secure channel or directly via e-RCS. Pay the statutorily prescribed registration fee. Attach the precise ISIC 5813 activity code and the list of lawful managers and signatories. The registry verifies the completed filing and assigns the RCS identification number, followed by a certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: RCS registration form (Formulaire de demande d’immatriculation)
List of managers and lawful signatories with identity documents
Registered-office address proof or domiciliation consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a deficiency query, the applicant must supply corrected or complementary documents within the deadline stated in the query, normally eight to fifteen days. If the query relates to the company name or object, file an amending notarial or administrative instrument and re-submit with the corresponding fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the electronic compendium of companies and associations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA), operated by the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the RCS has registered the deed, it automatically publishes the incorporation in the electronic compendium RESA. Verify the published reference, the RCS number, the managers’ names and the registered office. Download the official publication notice for use in banking and due diligence procedures.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA extract contains an inaccuracy, submit a prompt correction request to the RCSL with the authentic deed and a proposed corrected text. The registry will amend the public record and issue a rectified extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for corporate income tax; Administration de l’Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDTV) for VAT; central portal via Guichet.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply through the Guichet.lu business registration procedure for the Luxembourg business matriculation number (matricule). Register the company as a Luxembourg tax resident under the Income Tax Act, and obtain a VAT number if supplying electronic services. If employees are anticipated, simultaneously register as an employer with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS). Update the RCS file with any additional regulatory identifiers.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office lease or domiciliation agreement
Projected revenue and VAT declaration estimates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax administration challenges economic substance or effective management, provide the lease, utility invoices, bank statements, manager appointments and corporate decisions. File any required provisional corporate income tax return and, if challenged, submit a regularized VAT registration and proof of digital publishing activity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open corporate bank account and complete beneficial-owner registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institutions and the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs, RBE), Ministry of Justice, Luxembourg.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the RCS certificate, RESA publication, tax identification number and authentic articles to a Luxembourg bank to open the corporate operating account. Submit the detailed beneficial-ownership declaration to the RBE under the Law of 13 January 2019. Align the payment rails, including Stripe and AdSense payout parameters, with the bank’s compliance onboarding.
required_dossiers: Shareholders' register and ultimate beneficial owners schedule
Passport or ID of managers and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank’s AML/KYC unit rejects or delays account opening, provide sworn source-of-funds explanations, additional identification documents, and the final RBE receipt. If rejection persists, select an alternative Luxembourg credit institution and obtain pre-approval based on the fully prepared dossier.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – a digital magazine portal under ISIC 5813 is not an industrial activity requiring an establishment permit. If a physical office is occupied, the municipal authority (Administration communale) and the Ministry of the Environment have jurisdiction over local premises and waste compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating license or manufacturing permit is required for an online publishing activity under Luxembourg law. The Freedom to Provide Services and the RCS registration govern this activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l’Environnement, Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development, Luxembourg
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no physical project, no construction and no polluting facility within the meaning of the Luxembourg Law of 22 May 2008 on environmental impact assessment; the activity is fully digital and has no EIA threshold.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable. The business generates no significant wastewater, VOC emissions or hazardous waste streams. Office waste must be separated under municipal waste regulations, and end-of-life IT and data-centre equipment must be disposed of through authorized waste and WEEE channels.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire-safety clearance is mandatory for a virtual publishing operation. If a dedicated office is leased, the building owner must hold a valid fire-safety conformity certificate (certificat de sécurité incendie). Employer obligations are limited to affiliation with an approved occupational health service and completion of a workplace risk assessment in accordance with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 28 December 2016.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct taxes (corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net wealth tax), acting through the official portals impotsdirects.public.lu and myguichet.lu; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) for VAT (TVA) registration and indirect tax compliance, via aed.public.lu and myguichet.lu; Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS / Luxembourg Business Registers, lbr.lu) for company incorporation and business registration; Luxembourg Customs and Excise Agency for export-formalities and PLDA electronic customs declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Luxembourg SARL is incorporated before a notary, registered with the RCS and the Registre National des Sociétés et Associations (RNSA) to obtain the national business registration number (matricule, i.e., the RCS number and fiscal identification number), and is simultaneously registered with the ACD for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax. VAT registration is filed separately with the AED on the standard registration form, which leads to issuance of the Luxembourg VAT identification number (LV format). Non-resident entities establishing a Luxembourg branch must appoint a local authorized representative, register the branch with the RCS, and file the corresponding VAT and direct-tax registrations with the AED and the ACD; taxpayer identification is evidenced by the RCS matricule. EU-resident suppliers of cross-border B2C digital services may alternatively discharge Luxembourg VAT obligations through the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) without a full local VAT registration, while non-EU suppliers must either register directly in Luxembourg or identify themselves under the OSS regime through a selected EU member state and obtain a Luxembourg VAT identifier where supplies are made.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SARL is an autonomous corporate tax resident (société de capitaux) subject to corporate income tax (headline rate 17% plus a 7% solidarity surcharge), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal, aggregate standard combined rate 24.94% in Luxembourg City), and annual net wealth tax (0.5% on taxable net wealth exceeding EUR 500,000). Taxable scope is unlimited (worldwide income) for Luxembourg-resident companies, mitigated through double-tax treaties, the participation-exemption regime, and foreign-tax-credit relief; specific Territorial_Scope features apply to qualifying intra-group, outbound-dividend, capital-gains, and foreign-branch situations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists under Luxembourg law; entity classification is fixed by corporate and tax statutes. Available statutory elections and regimes include: (i) fiscal unity election (intégration fiscale) under Article 164bis LIR for Luxembourg-resident group companies held at least 95% by the elected parent; (ii) the opt-in participation-exemption regime under Article 166 LIR for qualifying shareholdings (≥10% or ≥EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost, held for an unbroken 12-month period and satisfying substance/subject-to-tax conditions); (iii) VAT group election (assujetti unique) under Article 60 of the VAT law; (iv) advance tax rulings (confirmatory rulings) from the ACD for financing arrangements, transfer pricing and hybrid-issue clearance; (v) the status of société de participations financières (SOPARFI) as a factual holding-company classification. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD are mandatory and do not provide elective carve-outs; hybrid arbitrage structures are statutorily disallowed.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA) — EU-harmonized value added tax with destination-based rules for electronically supplied services; no separate sales and use tax exists in Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 — Luxembourg imposes no general de minimis turnover threshold for VAT registration; any person carrying out taxable economic activities must register for VAT in Luxembourg. A small-business exemption applies under Article 57 of the VAT law only to resident taxable persons with annual turnover not exceeding EUR 35,000, and entails forfeiture of input-VAT recovery. Non-resident digital suppliers of B2C electronic services to Luxembourg consumers must register in Luxembourg unless they use the EU OSS regime; the EUR 10,000 annual Union-wide distance-sales and cross-border B2C digital-services threshold governs application of the supplier's home-state rules, with automatic registration in Luxembourg once exceeded. Intra-Community acquisition thresholds do not apply to a fully taxable Luxembourg SARL.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, software certification, or digital stamping mandate is currently in force in Luxembourg for standard B2B or B2C invoices; the AED does not operate a continuous transaction-control (CTC) clearance system. Invoices must satisfy Articles 34-36 of the VAT law (essential content, issuance, archiving for at least 6 years); e-invoicing is freely permitted, and the PEPPOL/EN 16931 format is mandatory for public-procurement (B2G) electronic invoicing. DAC7 digital-platform reporting applies to the operator of the digital magazine portal for reportable sellers. The EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) framework is expected to introduce mandatory structured e-invoicing and transaction-based digital reporting during the 2028-2030 implementation horizon; until then, the EC Sales List, Intrastat declarations, and OSS quarterly returns remain the operative compliance instruments.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods (including printed magazines, books, and physical publications) to destinations outside the EU qualify for the 0% VAT rate under Article 43 of the VAT law, provided the goods physically leave the EU within the statutory/administrative timeframe and the exit is proven by customs and transport documentation. Intra-EU supplies of goods to EU VAT-registered business customers are zero-rated where both parties hold valid VAT identification numbers, the customer's VAT number is confirmed in VIES, and EC Sales List / Intrastat reporting is rendered. Digital magazine subscriptions and electronically supplied advertising/media placements do not benefit from the classic customs export zero-rating: B2B e-services to non-EU customers fall outside Luxembourg VAT under the place-of-supply rules (Articles 44 and 45 of the VAT law) if the customer's business location and non-taxable status are evidenced; B2C digital services to EU consumers are taxed in the destination member state and reported through the OSS at the applicable foreign VAT rate; B2C digital services to non-EU consumers are outside Luxembourg VAT subject to two non-contradictory pieces of evidence of customer location (e.g., IP address, bank BIC country code, fixed-line country code). Zero-rating of advertising-media export services additionally requires a written contract demonstrating the economic link between the Luxembourg supplier, the non-EU customer, and the actual service provision outside Luxembourg.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EU Single Administrative Document / electronic export declaration filed in the Luxembourg PLDA customs clearance system)
Bill of Lading / CMR International Consignment Note / Air Waybill or equivalent proof of physical exit from the EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank SWIFT MT103 or equivalent payment-credit confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds in the SARL's bank account)
Commercial invoice and executed subscription, advertising, or digital-content contract
VAT registration numbers of both parties and EC Sales List records for intra-EU supplies
Customer-location evidence for digital services (IP address, bank country code, fixed-line country code, or two non-contradictory business-evidence items)
Franchise/platform payout records from Stripe and AdSense-payout rails evidencing the gross consideration, platform fees, and settlement currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AED may audit export zero-rating and OSS claims at any time during the standard five-year limitation period, requiring full documentary substantiation before the 0% rate is retained; where proof of physical export, customer location, or FX repatriation is deficient, the AED re-invoices the supply at the standard 17% VAT rate and levies late-payment interest at the statutory monthly accrual plus an administrative fine of up to EUR 250,000. Knowingly false zero-rating or fraudulent OSS declarations constitute VAT fraud, punishable by criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and/or imprisonment of up to five years, with joint and several liability of corporate directors and officers; the limitation period for reopening assessments is extended to ten years in cases of intentional evasion. Any input VAT provisionally refunded on the strength of an invalid export claim is clawed back with statutory interest from the date of refund. Although Luxembourg imposes no dedicated statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline, persistent non-repatriation of export receivables beyond the 180-day safe-harbor convention is treated by the ACD as a transfer-pricing red flag requiring arm's-length interest accruals, submission of transactional documentation, and potential double-counting of income in the corporate tax base; late repatriation must be supported by the underlying receivable ledger and FX controls in the SARL's transfer-pricing file.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting under the supervisory coordination of the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking conduct and AML/CTF compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: As a Eurozone member state, Luxembourg applies full convertibility for both current account and capital account transactions. The free movement of capital and payments is enshrined in Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU). Profit remittances, dividends, and capital repatriation are unrestricted and not subject to prior administrative authorization. However, financial counterparties must conduct transaction-level sanctions screening and verify the legitimate source of funds to mitigate money-laundering and terrorist-financing risks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory timeline or forced conversion ratio applies to export receipts in Luxembourg. Corporate entities may maintain foreign-currency accounts (e.g., USD, GBP) without any obligation to surrender or convert export earnings into EUR. All FX operations are executed freely in the interbank market at market-determined rates, provided the underlying transaction is declared for statistical purposes to the BCL when required under the EU balance of payments reporting framework.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for integrating EU/EEA-authorized Electronic Money Institutions (e.g., Stripe, Adyen, or Luxembourg-licensed EMIs) as payment service providers for merchant collection and disbursement. Legal constraints: (i) any EMI must be licensed under the EU Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and supervised by a European Economic Area (EEA) national authority; (ii) the EMI must not be used as a substitute for a corporate bank account for statutory capital deposits or balance sheet treasury; (iii) contracts must specify data residency and consumer-protection compliance for digital magazine subscriptions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is generally permitted via secure video conferencing (e.g., WebID, IDNow, or bank-specific electronic identity verification). Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs) and authorized signatories may be interviewed virtually; however, banks retain residual discretion to require an in-person visit for high-risk UBO structures. Luxembourg does not impose a statutory mandate for physical presence, but the bank must satisfy CSSF Circular 18/698 on KYC procedures. For this low-risk digital publishing entity, a fully remote procedure is viable if the furnished identity and corporate documentation are machine-verifiable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain involving multiple offshore entities or high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Full chain of incorporation chart and articles; (2) current Luxembourg Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) extract; (3) declarations of beneficial ownership signed by each UBO; (4) sanctions and PEP screening certificates from a reputable screening service; (5) notarized board resolution approving the banking relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound corporate funding exceeding EUR 15,000 from non-EEA sources
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Authenticated copy of the capital increase or shareholder loan agreement; (2) source-of-wealth evidence of each funding shareholder (bank statements, tax returns, audit report); (3) formal representation letter stating the absence of criminal funds and tax-avoidance intent; (4) ad-hoc compliance declarations mapping the counterparty through the EU sanctions list.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital advertising revenue flows from AdSense or programmatic ad networks with aggregated micropayments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Valid publisher agreements with Google and/or direct advertisers; (2) monthly revenue reconciliation reports; (3) contractual terms showing intellectual property ownership and commercial rationale; (4) clear breakdown of end-buyer jurisdictions if flagged for circumvention; (5) current data-protection impact assessment to demonstrate lawful consent for ad targeting.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfers must be routed via the SWIFT MT103 message type, with field 70 (Remittance Information) containing the purpose code 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'SUB

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts (comptes annuels) including balance sheet, P&L, non-financial disclosures and, where applicable, the auditor's report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); published by the Central Balance Sheet Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after financial year-end; for a calendar-year SARL, no later than June 30 following the closing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines from EUR 500 to EUR 5,000 per default; ongoing non-filing triggers RCS written summons, possible court-ordered compliance, and administrative or judicial dissolution/liquidation; directors may incur civil and tax liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Luxembourg corporate income tax return (déclaration d'impôt sur le revenu collectivités) including municipal business tax schedule and net wealth tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due within 6 months of year-end; when filed by an approved tax adviser, the ACD grants automatic extension to December 31 after the close of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Filing penalties up to EUR 5,000; late payment interest at 0.6% per month on due tax; additional tax assessment surcharges up to 10%; persistent default exposes officers to personal enforcement action

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer social declaration (état annuel des rémunérations) reconciling salaries, withholding and social security contributions by each employee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before January 31 following the calendar year to which the salaries relate; monthly contribution notices remain due separately on the 15th business day after the month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late declaration penalties up to EUR 1,000; unpaid employer contributions bear interest and may give rise to CCSS enforced recovery, including seizure of bank accounts and personal liability of directors

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the RCS legal data, directors, domiciliation and registered office details reflected in the commercial register extract
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)/Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before June 30 after the financial year-end, or concurrently with the annual accounts filing if the corporate data has changed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-updating of RCS data does not carry a separate annual fee but can lead to administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 and prevents legal reliance on RCS registration for the company and its officers

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SARL must appoint a certified independent auditor (réviseur d'entreprises) when it exceeds two of the following three criteria for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total over EUR 4.4 million, net turnover over EUR 8.8 million, and an average workforce over 50 employees; audit is also mandatory for public-interest entities, regulated financial-sector companies, funds and securitisations, and where shareholders holding more than 10% of capital or voting rights so request under Luxembourg law
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: LUX GAAP as transposed from EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU for unlisted SARLs; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is mandatory for consolidated accounts of market-listed companies and is permitted, with opt-in approval, for unlisted consolidated financial statements

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg maintains a central register of beneficial owners (RBE) accessible to the RCS; there is no free-standing annual UBO confirmation return, but the SARL must file any change in economic ownership or qualifying shareholding within 30 days of the event; a share transfer that changes beneficial control must be supported by a board resolution and updated UBO declaration at RCS, with director attestation accompanying the annual accounts confirming no undisclosed UBO changes have occurred

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 20,000 per annum for a digital publishing SARL; higher for group-owned or consolidated structures

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined headline rate for Luxembourg City (2024/2025): 17.00% CIT + 7.00% solidarity surcharge on CIT (1.19%) + 6.75% municipal business tax; rate varies with commune of establishment
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption: 100% of qualifying dividend and capital-gain income is exempt from CIT/IFL when ≥10% shareholding and a 12-month holding period is met; IP Box: 80% of net income from registered qualifying IP is exempt, effective CIT rate ≈ 4.9%; R&D credit: 20%/30% tax credit for qualified research expenditures and 44% credit for qualified researchers (EUR 54,000 cap) — subject to ACD approval
